basic_identification.full_title: SOLID CARBIDE PARALLEL SHANK TWIST DRILLS STUB SERIES — SPECIFICATION
basic_identification.sector_category: Cutting Tools Sectional Committee, PGD 32 (Approved and adopted under the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the dimensions, tolerances, and general requirements of solid carbide parallel shank twist drills in the stub series, designed primarily for right-hand cutting applications.

requirements.detail: Twist drills conforming to this standard must be manufactured specifically for right-hand cutting applications.

Solid carbide twist drills must be designated by the product name, stub series designation, nominal drill diameter, and carbide grade class conforming to this standard. Example: 'Twist Drill 6.00 K40 IS 16060'.
The dimensional tolerance applied to the overall length (l1) of the finished twist drill must belong to the 'very coarse' grade defined in IS 2102 (Part 1).
To prevent wobbling and uneven hole sizing during high-speed machining, the tolerance on the radial runout of the twist drill must be held strictly within 0.02 mm.
Enforces strict limits on the relative lip height tolerance to ensure even cutting force distribution on both lips.
The product may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Use is strictly regulated under the statutory provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16060 : 2013 is the national Indian Standard specification governing solid carbide twist drills of the stub series with parallel shanks, designed for high-performance right-hand metal cutting. Developed by the Cutting Tools Sectional Committee (PGD 32), this standard defines precise material grades (such as K40), a comprehensive sizing matrix (covering nominal diameters up to 20.00 mm, overall lengths, and flute lengths), and tight tolerances—including a maximum permissible radial runout limit of 0.02 mm and 'very coarse' length tolerances per IS 2102 (Part 1). It also maps out specific engineering surface roughness requirements, requiring an N6 finish on the shank and body, N7 on the point lips, and N9 inside the helical flutes to optimize chip flow.
